Assertions.Description: Clean-profile Settings/OOBE calls the module Shortcut Guide and describes the app-aware overlay, not V2.
Disabled from first render, with no transient Shortcut Guide process/event activation.
Enabling persists across a PowerToys restart.
The enabled Quick Access entry opens one full overlay without duplicate windows.
While disabled, Quick Access has no usable launch action and cannot open the overlay.
Re-enabling restores the Quick Access entry and its ability to open one full overlay.
Command Palette exposes the enabled module's **Toggle Shortcut Guide** command, which opens or toggles one full overlay without duplicate windows.
While Shortcut Guide is disabled, its settings entry remains, its toggle action is absent, and Command Palette cannot open the overlay.
Re-enabling restores the toggle entry and its ability to open or toggle the guide.
Settings displays **Win+Shift+/**.
That physical chord opens exactly one full overlay from the normal app.
The overlay displays the activation chord as key names/glyphs, not raw virtual-key numbers.
The captured Notepad page appears first and is selected, with its icon/name and app-specific shortcuts.
Each repeated page switch updates content and selection to the chosen application.
Taskbar indicators appear only on a page exposing them, including on the initial page before any switch.
After each page switch, the overlay remains open with the selected page's content, without a crash or a blank page.
Each Windows recommendation appears once under **Recommended** and once in its original category, with no additional copies.
Meta-section names such as `<TASKBAR1-9>` are not rendered literally; taskbar shortcuts have their localized heading.
**Peek at desktop temporarily** renders as **Win+,**.
**Open Click to Do** renders as **Win+Q**.
The unused custom SG chord persists across Settings close/reopen.
After Settings close/reopen, the new chord opens the guide; the old **Win+Shift+/** chord no longer opens it.
The custom binding still works after the explicit PowerToys restart.
After restart, the PowerToys page displays the exact customized SG chord.
Before any restart, ordinary opening displays the representative module's exact custom modifiers/key instead of its default.
Ordinary reopening after resetting that module displays the restored binding, without requiring a restart.
Restore **Win+Shift+/** for the test, and preserve the captured original binding for final state restoration.
**Off** persists in Settings.
Neither indicators nor the full guide appears for either key's tap or long hold in Off mode.
Normal short-press Start behavior remains available in Off mode.
The independent configured activation chord still opens the full guide in Off mode.
Full-guide mode with close-on-release enabled persists.
A beyond-duration hold opens the full guide for either Windows key.
Release closes it without leaving Start, taskbar indicators or a second overlay visible.
Full-guide mode with close-on-release disabled persists.
The hold-opened guide remains after release.
Escape closes that same retained guide, before any cleanup closes it.
The independent configured chord opens and toggles the guide with close-on-release off.
Indicator mode and the distinctive valid duration persist.
Both keys show no indicators before the threshold and show only indicators, not the full guide, beyond it.
Releasing each activated plain hold hides indicators without opening Start.
Both the control and saved JSON clamp below-range input to 100 and above-range input to 5,000.
The three tracked apps occupy the observed known slots.
One numbered indicator aligns with each eligible taskbar button without overlap, with its tail pointing toward the current taskbar edge.
Held Win+1 brings the exact first-slot app foreground.
After releasing `1`, Windows is still held, indicators remain visible, and Start stays closed.
Releasing Windows closes the indicators without opening Start.
A fresh guide closes once with Escape, leaves no orphan overlay and supports the next invocation.
A fresh guide closes once with the configured chord, leaves no orphan overlay and supports the next invocation.
A fresh guide closes once with its title-bar Close button, leaves no orphan overlay and supports the next invocation.
A fresh guide closes once when clicking the transparent area outside the pane, leaves no orphan overlay and supports the next invocation.
A fresh guide closes once when another tracked app becomes foreground, leaves no orphan overlay and supports the next invocation.
The configured physical chord opens the non-elevated guide above an elevated Notepad fixture.
A safe displayed Windows shortcut such as Win+E opens the expected Explorer fixture and closes the guide; close only that Explorer fixture.
With notepad.exe excluded and the fixture foreground, the configured chord opens no guide surface.
With notepad.exe excluded and the fixture foreground, the configured Windows-key action opens no guide surface.
With the exclusion still present, foreground Explorer and confirm the guide opens.
Remove the exclusion and confirm Notepad activation works without restarting Windows.
After warm-up, ten open/navigate/close cycles reuse the same PID with functional navigation/content and at most one visible overlay in each cycle.
Private working set after the ten cycles and two-second idle increases by no more than 32 MiB from the warm baseline.
Desktop activation succeeds without a blank-title fault.
Windows and PowerToys vector rail entries are readable and one is selected.
Selected page has Pinned, Recommended where applicable, normal headings and shortcut key caps.
The rail Settings icon is fully visible; invoking it opens the existing Settings window directly to Shortcut Guide.
Pin from a row context menu creates one Pinned row and records it for the correct application in Pinned.json.
The row remains pinned after dismissing and reopening the guide.
Unpin removes the row immediately and restores localized empty-state text; restore the original Pinned.json.
After backing up and removing the per-user shortcuts directory, guide invocation recreates the directory and index.
Every bundled manifest in the tested build is copied and referenced exactly once; every copied YAML parses.
Windows, PowerToys, Explorer and Notepad pages remain available without a launch crash; restore the original directory.
A disposable Notepad-filtered manifest renders virtual-key 65, <1>, <LessThan>, <GreaterThan> and an arrow as A, 1, <, > and the expected arrow glyph/name, not raw numbers/tokens.
Empty and unknown keys in that manifest neither crash the guide nor suppress valid sibling shortcuts.
A name-text probe matches case-insensitively.
A separate description-text probe matches case-insensitively.
A modifier-name probe matches case-insensitively.
An isolated displayed-key-label probe matches case-insensitively.
Only matching rows and their section headings remain; empty sections disappear.
The query filters only the selected application page and is retained/reapplied when switching pages.
Ctrl+F moves focus to the search box, which has an accessible name.
No-match input shows a localized polite live-region message with no stale shortcut rows.
The first Escape clears the query without closing the guide.
The next Escape closes that guide.
Normal reopening starts with an empty query.
Selected rail items expose their selected state.
Each opening, including the two repeated openings per mode, uses one readable theme across the pane, transparent host, key caps, selection indicators, icons, search, taskbar indicators and text.
After a Windows app-theme change in system mode, the next opening follows that theme.
Both Left and Right settings persist.
After opening, the pane is on the selected side.
Its shadow and rounded acrylic surface are not clipped.

One transparent guide host covers the selected monitor's work area (RcWork, excluding taskbar/reserved space) in physical virtual-screen coordinates, without a duplicate host or a second DPI scaling. Full monitor bounds are not the expected rectangle.
Shortcut Guide creates no taskbar button.
Shortcut Guide creates no Alt+Tab entry.
After changing to a supported non-English PowerToys language and restarting, Shortcut Guide Settings labels are localized without resource keys or unintended English fallback.
Title, search, Close, Settings, Pinned, Recommended, Taskbar, Pin/Unpin and no-results text are localized; application-manifest names/descriptions may remain English. Restore the original language.

With different DPI scales on two monitors, foreground Notepad on each in turn: full guide appears on that foreground monitor, stays within its work area and has no double scaling, gap, spill or cross-monitor offset.
On each differently scaled monitor in turn, taskbar-indicator mode appears on the foreground monitor within its work area and aligns to its taskbar without double scaling, gap, spill or offset.
